questions.stem: What is an agent according to the text?
options: A model that only turns text into text.
A model using tools in a loop.
A model that runs commands without feedback.
A model that runs code without context.
questions.source_quote: > An agent is a model using tools in a loop.

questions.stem: What does the tool loop in an agent do?
options: It runs the model's code without feedback.
It feeds results back to the model for the next step.
It checks if the model's work is correct.
It decides the model's next action without context.
questions.source_quote: > The tool loop does the work. The feedback loop checks it.

questions.stem: How does the feedback loop differ from the tool loop in an agent?
options: The feedback loop runs the model's code without context.
The feedback loop feeds results back to the and decides the next step.
The feedback loop checks the output against a specification.
The feedback loop runs the model's code without feedback.
questions.source_quote: > The feedback loop is around the whole agent. A check compares the output with the specification, and the error goes back in as the next input.

questions.stem: What is the role of checks in an agent system?
options: They run the model's code without feedback.
They ensure the model's work meets a specification.
They decide the model's next action without context.
They run the model's code without context.
questions.source_quote: > Checks are things like tests, type checkers, linters and schema validation. They are deterministic and cheap.

questions.stem: What is the harness in an agent system?
options: The model that runs the code without feedback.
The deterministic code that controls the agent's behavior.
The model that decides the next action without context.
The code that runs the model's code without context.
questions.source_quote: > The harness is everything that is not the model. It is deterministic code, and it is where engineering happens.
